text:
anya: FYI rolled the canary for runtime change d4f7c3 ~10:33, seeing memory spikes and OOMs on long-context workloads (seqlen 8k+). High-priority, can we gate?

deploy-bot: Deployed r/runtime@d4f7c3 to canary group-b at 10:33 (sha d4f7c3).

mike: Reproduced locally with a canary profile. KV hot-slab grew steadily after ~2k tokens, peak +140MB vs baseline. Fragmentation up, free-chunks count down. Quick snippet from slab stats:```hot_slab: +142MB
free_chunks: 312 -> 94
alloc_failures: 0 (so far)
kv_live_items: +18%```

jordan: Bisecting points at commit 9f2b7a — kernel-router: change from contiguous alloc -> slab-striping + alignment tweak. Also autobatch change in same merge increased max_concurrency default from 6->8. Either could amplify seqlen-sensitive memory.

anya: 9f2b7a was included in d4f7c3. Good find. Is this more alloc pattern or cache pressure?

mike: Profiling heap shows many small VC entries persisted in warmup window. The striping increases number of active heaplets per request, autobatch concurrency multiplies that. So per-request steady-state footprint up.

ci-bot: CI job "kv-memory-stability" failed on PR checks for d4f7c3: peak-rss +22% on seqlen=8192 test. Log: https://ci/redwood/job/kv-memory-stability/4623 (excerpt above).

jordan: Hypothesis: allocator alignment + stripe-sharding changed placement, causing higher fragmentation and preventing coalescing on eviction. Combined with larger concurrent batches we hit more live warmup entries => apparent leak-ish behavior.

anya: Proposed mitigations: 1) pin kernel-router to previous route (revert allocator alignment) 2) temporarily reduce autobatch max_concurrency 8->4 3) enable more aggressive KV compact-on-evict for canaries. Which is lowest-risk to push?

samir: I'll open a revert PR for the allocator tweak only (keeping the other perf changes). Will also add a smoke CI that exercises seqlen=8192. PR: #2314.

samir: Pushed revert PR 1769501001 - revert allocator alignment tweak, added a flag to toggle striping. Requesting urgent review from eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy of revert PR to canary group-b: started 10:58, instances 1/5 updated.

mike: Also pushing a hotfix to reduce autobatch concurrency in canary config now: set runtime.autobatch.max_concurrency=4. Doing that while revert rolls.

anya: Monitoring dashboards (memory, slab_free_chunks, kv_active_items) — link: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-runtime/canary-memory. If we don't see memory drop within 15m post-deploy, escalate and rollback to previous artifact (pre-d4f7c3).

jordan: For postmortem: add a synthetic long-ctx load test to the perf suite (seqlen 8k/16k) and a slab-frag metric to CI. Also add a canary-only compact-on-evict toggle.

ci-bot: Noted. Created issue #ENG-8890 "add seqlen-8k synthetic and slab-frag check".

anya: Thanks all. Assigning follow-ups: samir (revert PR + monitor), mike (observability dashboards + compact toggle), jordan (postmortem checklist). Will reconvene in 20m. :hourglass: 

samir: Update: after first 3 instances of revert, memory dropped ~60MB on avg per instance, free_chunks recovering. Continuing rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy to canary complete 11:15 — 5/5 instances updated. Monitoring for 30m.

anya: Great progress. Leave the autobatch fix in place for now until we verify long-run stability. If stable after 1h we'll promote to prod. :thumbsup:
